feature_notes: HydraBudget literals for Droppy-run heads: pacingTools = 24, wrapUpTools = 120, maxTools = 160, wrapUpSeconds = 25 * 60, maxSeconds = 35 * 60, reportSeconds = 3 * 60

HydraBudget.pacingNote exact text: "[Droppy Code] You have run 24 tools without changing a file. If the task is research, reply with your findings now. Otherwise act on what you know: make the change, or reply with what blocks you." (the 24 is interpolated from pacingTools)
HydraBudget.wrapUpNote: "[Droppy Code] Your budget is nearly spent. Finish now: complete the smallest correct version of the task, then reply with your report."
HydraBudget.finalNote: "[Droppy Code] Your budget is spent and your tools are gone. Reply now with your report: what you changed, how far it got, and what is left."

Concurrency: a pair's maxHeads is clamped to 1...8 on decode; with no cap, HydraLaunch.uncappedConcurrency = 8 heads run at once and the rest wait (comment cites 21 simultaneous heads forcing a force quit)

maxDelegationRounds = 3 rounds of heads per user request; heldBackMessage(count:) says "Hydra held back a head." / "Hydra held back N heads." then "None of the heads you asked for went out: this request has had all 3 of its rounds of heads already. Do the rest yourself now, without git status or git diff on the heads' work, and answer the user."
Native providers with their own heads: .claude, .codex, .copilot (the switch in policy(for:) and in howToSpawn); everything else gets the fenced hydra fallback block

Claude spawn wording: "Two agent types are yours: `droppy-worker` (edits files, runs commands) and `droppy-scout` (read-only research). Spawn them with the Agent tool..."; Codex: "Spawn heads with `spawn_agent`: the `worker` agent ... the `explorer` agent for read-only research."; Copilot: "Two agents are yours ... Start them with the task tool ..."

Claude wait wording: "Launch every head for a job in one message so they run in parallel, in the foreground" + ", and run at most N at once."; Codex adds " Run at most N at once."; Copilot adds ", and run at most N at a time."

Native agent JSON: claudeAgents sets "background": false for both agents, gives the scout tools ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "WebFetch", "WebSearch"], skips model when it equals "default" and skips effort when empty; profile variants are named droppy-worker-<agentSlug>

copilotAgents sets "infer": true, skips model when it equals "auto", uses "reasoningEffort", displayName "Hydra worker" / "Hydra scout" / "Hydra worker · <profile name>", and deliberately passes no tools list for the scout (a tool name the CLI does not know could refuse the whole session)
codexConfig only exposes features.multi_agent_v2.expose_spawn_agent_model_overrides when nativeRoutableProfiles is non-empty; features.multi_agent is always true
nativeRoutableProfiles filters to profiles whose provider is nil or equals launch.headsProvider AND that set a model or an effort
profileName(forAgentName:) strips the "droppy-worker-" prefix; "droppy-worker" and "droppy-scout" route nowhere (nil)

Roster naming discipline in the prompts: the lead is told the full 25-name order and told "There is no head called Ives; the roster has Ivo."; HydraRoster.index(named:) matches case-insensitively, strips a trailing integer round suffix, and returns nil for unknown names so an announcement never renames a stranger
HydraRoster.persona(named:) honours the round suffix: "Nova 3" resolves to persona(at: index + 2 * 25)

Fence parsing: delegationOpener matches ```[ \t]*hydra(?:-sent|-leaving)?[ \t]*\r?\n case-insensitively; delegationBlockRange runs to the LAST line-starting ``` after the opener (never the first, because a prompt may quote its own fence), or to endIndex while still streaming

delegations(in:) retries parsing with each candidate closing fence from last back to first, then the end of text; an empty JSON array parses to [] (no heads, not nil); entries with no usable prompt are dropped
withoutDelegationBlock(_:) removes the block range and trims whitespace/newlines

unreadableBlockMessage(reason:) prefix "[Hydra] Your delegation block could not be read, so no heads went out." plus an optional reason (a period is appended unless it already ends in . ! or ?) plus the re-write instructions ending "This does not count as a round of heads."

verificationMarkers (34 exact substrings, lowercased match): "xcodebuild", "swift build", "swift test", "swiftlint", "npm test", "npm run build", "npm run test", "yarn build", "yarn test", "pnpm test", "cargo build", "cargo test", "go test", "pytest", "gradle", "eslint", "tsc " (trailing space), "build succeeded", "run the build", "run the tests", "run the test suite", "build and prove", "prove it builds", "prove it compiles", "check that it builds", "check it still builds", "make sure it builds", "make sure it compiles", "confirm the build", "verify the build", "verify that it builds", "make sure nothing else broke", "run the suite", "build verification"
withoutVerificationSteps(_:) drops any line containing a marker and, only when something was dropped, appends "\nMake the assigned edits and report; the lead handles all validation."

delegatedHeadPrompt sections in order: "You are <Name>, a Hydra head in Droppy Code: one of several helpers working in parallel for a lead agent. The lead delegated this task to you.", "## Your task: <task>", "## Where you work", "## How to work", "## Your report"

queuedHeadPrompt sections: "## What is going on in the main chat", "## Your task", "## Where you work", "## How to work", "## Your report"; context lines quote the last user prompt to 1200 characters and the lead's last reply to 800, both in curly quotes with a trailing … when cut, and list at most 20 touched paths; leadIsWorking toggles "The user queued this task for you while the lead works on something else." versus "The user sent this task straight to you; the lead is idle and will hear your report."; empty context gives "The lead has not said anything yet."

workplaceRules .ownCopy tells the head it has a git worktree made from the checkout as it was when it was sent out, uncommitted work included, and forbids commit/branch/stash/push/checkout/reset/restore/clean and worktree creation, plus "Never build, test or verify anything in your copy"
workplaceRules .shared tells the head it shares the lead's checkout with other heads and forbids git status / git diff self-checks
reportMessage opening: "Hydra reports: <list> finished." and, with heads still out, "<list> is/are still at work; its report comes/their reports come as a later message."

reportMessage closings include: "The changes listed above are in your checkout already; nothing needs applying.", "The heads worked in your checkout, so their changes are there already.", the conflict line, a per-file warning when two heads changed the same path ("<A> and <B> both changed <path>: read it as it is now before you build on it."), "<Name>'s changes would not apply on their own; the patch is at <path>. Apply it with `git apply --3way <path>` and settle what conflicts.", the failed-head line, the stopped-head line, the queued-origin line and the sent-origin line
duration(_:) formats "<n>s" under 60 seconds and "<m>m <s>s" above
list(_:) joins with commas and a final " and "

fallbackPolicy opens "[Hydra is on] You lead a team of up to N helper agents (\"heads\")." (or "a team of helper agents" with no cap) and instructs the lead to end its reply with one ```hydra fenced JSON array; it explicitly warns that three backticks inside a prompt would end the block early and to indent snippets by four spaces instead

fallbackPolicy names the exact entry shapes: {"task": "...", "prompt": "..."}, with optional "name" (announced, authoritative) and "project" (sidebar name or path), and with profiles present a "profile" key demonstrated as {"task": "...", "prompt": "...", "profile": "<first profile name>"}
fallbackPolicy notes each entry dispatches "the moment its closing brace streams, before the block is finished"
isolatesHeads wording: "Each head works in a copy of its project of its own and Droppy Code lands its changes in that project's checkout when it reports" versus "The heads work in your checkout"

delegationRequest(_:) emits "[Hydra setting: enabled]" followed by routing guidance that differs by launch.runsNatively, ending with "

---

"

fallbackTurnNote / fallbackReportNote prefix "[Hydra] " and end with "

---

"; the report note offers another round only when canDelegate, otherwise "Send out no more heads for this request; whatever is left, do yourself."

mergeStatus handles three HydraMergeRecord outcomes: .merged ("the team's work already merged as <label> <url> in <project> at <time> (N files)."), .failed ("the last merge failed at <time>: <detail or 'no reason recorded'>..."), .stray (footnote after the last successful merge, default detail "files were changed outside every project"); with no merges and no unmerged files it returns nil
autoMergeRule forbids the lead from running or delegating branch/commit/merge-request operations and from claiming a merge the [Hydra] note does not confirm
reviewRule has the lead read every changed file named in reports plus affected callers, fix integration issues itself, run the narrowest required build, and never delegate the review
reportStyleRule demands one plain sentence per head starting with its name, no audit jargon and no decorative symbols

files.purpose: The curated catalogue of ten ready-made Hydra lead/heads pairings ('recipes') offered in the UI, written in terms of model names rather than providers, plus two helpers: one that keeps a wanted effort only when the resolved ModelOption actually offers it, and one that tells whether an equivalent pair is already configured.

feature_notes: Only one recipe caps concurrency: "claude-opus-gemini-flash" with maxHeads = 6; the other nine leave maxHeads nil (uncapped, so HydraLaunch.uncappedConcurrency = 8 applies)
Effort literals used across the table: "high", "medium", "max", or nil to keep the provider default

Every model-name list is ordered best-first and falls back through broader fragments ("Gemini 3.8 Flash" then "Gemini" then "Flash"; "V4.1 Flash" then "V4.1" then "DeepSeek"; "5.3 Flash" then "GLM"); a recipe whose names find nothing in any installed provider's catalog is not offered at all
Provider lists are ordered so a model's own house wins over an aggregator: .commandcode is always listed last except in recipe 5 (.cursor only) and recipe 6 heads (.meta, .commandcode)
effort(_:for:) returns the wanted effort only when option.efforts contains it, otherwise nil so the model's default effort stands
isAdded(_:in:) considers a pair a duplicate when provider, headsProvider, orchestratorModel and workerModel all match; efforts, maxHeads, name and headProfiles are deliberately not compared
unresolved_questions: How a recipe's model-name fragments are matched against a provider catalog (case sensitivity, prefix versus substring) is decided by code outside this bundle
The mapping from a chosen recipe to a concrete HydraPair (which provider is picked when several serve the model) is also outside this file

files.purpose: Incremental parsing of a lead's ```hydra delegation block while the reply is still streaming, so each head is dispatched the moment its JSON entry's outermost brace closes. Provides a stateless whole-text/whole-body reader (HydraPrompts.streamedDelegations), the shared single-entry reader HydraPrompts.delegation(fromEntry:) that the non-streaming parser in Hydra.swift also uses, and a stateful byte-at-a-time HydraDelegationStreamParser class that ingests only newly appended text.

persisted_fields: None persisted. The JSON field names consumed from a delegation entry are: "prompt" (required, trimmed, must be non-empty), "task" (optional, trimmed), "name" with fallback "head" (optional announced roster name), "project" with fallback "repo" (optional), "profile" (optional head-profile name)
ui_elements: No UI. The only user-visible literal produced is the head's task title when no "task" was given: TextCleanup.singleLine(prompt, limit: 60), i.e. a 60-character single-line title derived from the prompt
feature_notes: streamedDelegations(in:) recognises only ```hydra and ```hydra-sent info strings (not ```hydra-leaving, unlike delegationOpener in Hydra.swift which also accepts -leaving)

streamedDelegations(inBody:) skips leading JSON whitespace (space, \n, \r, \t), then requires '[' (array, cursor advances past it) or '{' (one bare entry, cursor stays); any other first byte returns an empty, incomplete result

Termination conditions that set isComplete: ']' at depth 0, a '`' that opens a line at depth 0 (the closing fence), a '}' driving depth below 0 (broken block), or the closing '}' of a bare single entry

Each entry is parsed with JSONValue.parse on the substring from its opening brace to its closing brace inclusive; an entry that does not parse or that delegation(fromEntry:) rejects is silently skipped, so the streaming and whole-block parsers agree on order and count
atLineStart starts true because the body begins right after the opening fence's newline, and is updated as `byte == \n` after each byte
HydraDelegationStreamParser.ingest ignores further text once isComplete and breaks out of the byte loop as soon as isComplete flips

readOpener is a hand-written 16-state ASCII machine: states 0...2 count backticks (96), state 3 skips space (32) and tab (9) and extra backticks and requires 'h' (lowercased 104), states 4...7 require 'y' (121), 'd' (100), 'r' (114), 'a' (97), state 8 accepts '-' (45) to enter states 9...12 requiring 's' (115), 'e' (101), 'n' (110), 't' (116); states 13/14 accept trailing space/tab, '\r' (13) moves to state 15, '\n' (10) enters the body; a stray backtick anywhere resets the cursor to 1 rather than 0
The streaming class therefore accepts only ```hydra and ```hydra-sent, matching streamedDelegations(in:) and not the -leaving variant

readBody mirrors the stateless walk with raw ASCII codes: 34 '"', 92 '\\', 91 '[', 93 ']', 96 '`', 123 '{', 125 '}'; the entry accumulator is appended to only while depth > 0 and reset to [byte] on the outermost '{'
The class doc states it reads only newly appended UTF-8 bytes; completed or replaced messages get a fresh parser, and the runtime's sent watermark prevents already dispatched entries repeating

delegation(fromEntry:) drops an entry with a missing, non-string or whitespace-only "prompt"; an empty "task" is replaced by the 60-character single-line prompt title; empty-string name/project/profile are normalised to nil
The "name" an entry carries is passed through as-is for the spawner to resolve against the roster; an unknown "profile" falls back to the pair's shared worker model
unresolved_questions: The class's turnID and entryID are stored but never read inside this file; their use (keying the parser per streaming message) is in the runtime outside this bundle

The exact behaviour of JSONValue.parse on a truncated or malformed entry (throwing versus nil) is assumed to be nil-returning from the optional binding, but JSONValue.swift was not read in this bundle
